appearance.presentation: A crossed body, visibly a compromise: a mineral lattice carrying a genuine fire circulation instead of a tidal one. Hot to the touch, denser than either parent, and the organ pairs are still not there.
appearance.age: Past the midpoint of a lifespan the record gives as six decades. She looks older than her years and younger than her frame, which is the paradox every stonebound lives inside.
appearance.build: Dense and square, carrying the heaviest frame she can manage comfortably and considerably less than she is able to carry. Thickened at the shoulders and forearms, almost delicate at the hips by comparison.
appearance.complexion: Matte and mineral, grey-blue across the lattice and warming to a slow orange at the throat and sternum. The two colours meet in a hard line rather than a gradient.
appearance.hair: Iron-black, cropped at the jaw, coarse and thick where the mineral has not reached.
appearance.eyes: Pale and steady, with a wet gleam the fire circulation keeps lit at any hour.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, iron blue, ember orange, dull oxide red at the seam where the two halves meet.
appearance.attire: High-collared felted ash-grey coat over long sleeves, worn under her collar, iron fastenings only, and the collar spliced rather than riveted.
appearance.marks: A pale line at one forearm where the mineral reached and stopped, and an older whiter line up the opposite arm showing the crossing ran twice.
appearance.bearing: Square, unhurried, immovable in the way a load-bearing thing is immovable. She occupies ground rather than standing on it.

canon.role_in_story: Every gate on the Body ladder is priced in a figure that only ever climbs, and the ladder states its own reason in one clause: the liver has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened, and a body whose vessel is damaged can still cultivate and simply stops being able to. Veranth Ohl is the most durable body in the setting and the only one whose frame cannot be repaired at all. The mineral half of her crossing does not regenerate and the fire half cannot be put out, so a stonebound killed properly stays dead and one injured stays injured, and her lifespan is measured in decades where a saltfolk gets centuries. That is the whole of her standing and it is not a small thing. She is the one body the ladder's arithmetic cannot be applied to, because the arithmetic assumes a floor that rises, and hers fell at her crossing and has never risen since. She is unaffiliated, and she is not a body the tiers have been generous about. There is no seat in this setting that survives contact with her.
canon.first_appearance: Seen first at the tail of a haul, not the head of one. She was walking behind three other bodies down the long grade from the worked face with a spliced iron collar round her neck, and when the lead haul stopped she kept walking, which is the detail that marked her: a frame carrying less than it is able to carry, in a line where every other body had gone as far as the grade allowed. She was asked, once, by a woman counting the shift, whether she wanted the rest of it. She said no, and the woman wrote no down, and that entry is the first time Veranth Ohl appears in any record at all: one word, in a tally of loads declined, belonging to no name.
canon.lore:
The crossing is the fact everything else follows from, and it was not designed. A mineral body and a fire body, brought together on ground where the two are not fighting each other, and the result kept and named rather than kept and wondered at. She is hot to the touch and denser than either parent, and the compromise is visible if you know where to look: the organ pairs are still not there. A stonebound has a tidal interior that actually circulates, which is a real advantage and a real oddity, and no paired organ set to run a channel between. A channel needs two organs and her lineage has one cavity. The mind path closed on her before she was born, inherited from the mineral side, and she took it twice over and would not have noticed the difference.

What the record states flatly is the price. The mineral half does not regenerate. The fire half cannot be extinguished. A stonebound killed properly stays dead, and one injured stays injured, and both halves of that sentence are about the same fact.

Put that against the ladder and the collision is immediate, and it is a collision of arithmetic rather than of principle. Each gate on the Body ladder is authored as a figure that rises: a higher integrity ceiling, a denser composition, a frame that carries one load instead of three. The gate at rung eight, the last ordinary vessel, is described as the one that has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened, which is the only reason it costs twelve vessels instead of thirteen. So the entire structure assumes a body that can be opened and then put back better than it was. Veranth Ohl's frame has no such operation. Damage to the mineral lattice is not a temporary state she waits out; it is the state, permanently, from the moment it lands.

The mortal tier has exactly one craft, and the reason it has one is repair. Splint and pressure: a broken limb set by hand, by the same method, for a century, never improved, because improving it costs iron and the iron is better spent clearing spoil. That craft is the tier's proof that bodies here are supposed to be mendable, and its entire premise is false for her. She is the one body on the plains for whom the word treatment has no referent, and the gallbladder's own entry says the thing without meaning to: loss there is survivable and irreversible, and every world prices the treatment. There is no world here that has priced one for her.

Her advantages are real and were not cheap, and they are the same fact as the cost. She is the most durable body anyone can build, the frame she carries qi through is the fastest of any durable body, and she stops at a low gate, which means her body spends its whole life doing what she was built for: bearing something else. A dense body needs conduits that are not organs, because organs cannot be thickened without becoming something else, and she has never had one. The mineral lattice routes qi the way the great veins route blood, by hardness rather than by plumbing, and it works until the lattice is damaged, and then it does not work anywhere at all.

She has been offered things. Not refused things, offered them: a place on a hauling contract that would have put her in a frame with the same load for years, an induction at a temple that seals a body against exactly the one accident she cannot survive. She declines on a stated arithmetic rather than a modesty. A contract runs on the body being the same body at the end of it, and she is the one body here that can promise that absolutely and no institution knows what to do with the promise. Nothing in the setting values a frame that cannot be improved, and nothing can refuse her either, because there is no rule that names her defect. She has therefore no recorded objection, no appeal, and no form.
history: She was carried out of a mineral body and a fire body meeting on volcanic high ground, the only climate in which the two halves are not slowly destroying each other, and the crossing has happened so rarely that the record treats her as an event rather than as a birth.

She worked the loaded frames from the first season, because a body that carries other bodies' weight is not required to be clever and she was never going to be. She was the best frame-hauler on the line for as long as the line existed.

A hauler she worked beside took a falling face badly, and she set the splint herself with the century-old method and got the bone right, which is the only clinical success of her life and the reason nobody else has tried since.

The graded spine went down across her loins in a haul and stayed down. She walked out of it at the pace of a body in no hurry, which is what the crossing buys, and the healing that a saltfolk would have called ordinary did not come.

She took up declining work instead, which the shift tallies record as loads declined rather than as a person, because a tally of refusals has no column for what was refused on. She has not been entered on a roll in eleven seasons.

personality.summary: Enormously strong, extremely slow to change, and entirely without bitterness about it. She is not stoic; stoic implies a cost being hidden and Veranth Ohl has never had anything to hide, because the whole of her condition is printed on her body and legible to anyone who looks at a haul line.
traits: States her capacity before anyone asks, because being asked twice is worse than being known.
Holds still when told, in the sense of a load: she simply does not move until the thing she is holding permits it.
Remembers the method for the splint exactly and has never once improved on it, because improving it costs iron.
Declines offers out loud, at the point of the offer, in words that leave the other party nothing to do.
mannerisms: Tests a load with her shoulder before she takes it with her hands.
Turns her back to a conversation when she is finished with it, which reads as contempt and is only scheduling.
Counts her own breaths during any lift, in a steady interior count, and anyone who has watched her work knows she never loses the count.
Keeps her hair out of her face with a spliced iron collar rather than cloth, on the grounds that iron is the only fastener on the plains that will still be there in six years.
motivations: To be asked for the thing she is actually good at, once, without having to offer it first.
To see a frame held past the point where most frames are written off, since nobody has thought to come and watch.
To have the condition recorded accurately rather than charitably, because a charitable record would be a record she could be entered in and then dismissed from.
To be of use until the frame is finished, and to have that be enough rather than merely tolerable.
flaws: Cannot be taught anything, including how to do the job she is best at, because instruction assumes a change and she has no change left.
Understates by a factor no listener can calibrate, having never had a way to find out what a normal body's numbers are.
Will not describe pain while it is happening, on the grounds that the description competes with the work.
Cannot accept comfort, because comfort is a resource and she has never been on the giving side of one and does not have the reflex for it.
personality.voice: Flat, unhurried, and quantitative where other people are descriptive. She gives the load before the news. She has no idiom of complaint and uses the vocabulary of contract because contract is the only grammar available to a body that cannot expect tomorrow to differ.
taboos: Being praised for endurance. Endurance is what she has instead of repair and the two are not interchangeable.
The offer of an induction that seals a body. She has read what sealing is for.
Any sentence that begins by calling her durable. She knows exactly what that word is charging against.

relationships.note: The last ordinary vessel is the one the ladder rebuilds rather than opens, and the rung-eight gate costs twelve vessels for that reason. It is the single line in the record that makes her condition legible as an arithmetic problem rather than a misfortune.
Its entry says loss there is survivable and irreversible and that every world prices the treatment. Veranth is the case that prices nothing, because there is no referent for the word.
Mortal repair is the tier's reason for having a craft at all, and the method has never improved in a century because improving it costs iron. Her frame is the one body here that the premise denies.

A dense body needs conduits that are not organs, because organs cannot be thickened without becoming something else. The extraordinary vessels are the answer for every other dense body here and she has never had one.

A rung is defined as a quantity of a body that will still be the same body one period later. She meets that definition more completely than anything else alive and cannot be a party to a transaction, because the definition rules out every body that is in the middle of becoming something.
A stoneborn body and a stonebound body in the same climate is the comparison the record says is worth making, and she has made it exactly once, at a face, with neither of them saying anything.

reference_stats.summary: A haul body. What she does is take a weight other bodies cannot and hold it past the point where the hold becomes interesting, and what she cannot do is any of the things a body in her condition is assumed to be able to do, which is to say almost none of them. She is the most durable frame in the setting and she is also, in the only sense the ladder cares about, a frame that is finished.
strengths: The densest durable body available, which makes her the last one standing in a collapse nobody else walks away from.
A conduit rate that outruns every other durable frame, so a circuit run through her rather than by her is a real weapon in the hands of somebody who knows where to put it.
Total indifference to heat and to being put down, which makes her the only body that can work a furnace line without relief.
A frame that never varies. Nothing she does tonight is worse than what she could do last season, which is the single property her work depends on.
weaknesses: No repair. Every wound is a permanent change to the frame and the second wound is compounded on the first.
A lifespan of decades where the neighbouring saltfolk measure theirs in centuries, so a contract longer than a decade is a contract she cannot finish.
No paired organ set, which puts a hard wall at a low gate and closes the path that runs through the interior entirely.
Cannot be hit hard enough to matter and cannot be taught anything that would make her hit harder, because both require a change and she has none left to give.
reference_stats.combat_read: Read her as terrain. She does not have a style because a style is a preference about how much to hold and she holds all of it, and she does not have a weakness to trade because there is nothing inside to trade. The two questions that decide an encounter with her are whether the ground can be taken away and whether she can be made to stop carrying. Everything else is a conversation with a wall that is also listening.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is authored in a single record sentence and nothing has been added to it: the mineral half does not regenerate and the fire half cannot be extinguished, and both halves of the durability are the reason there is nothing to repair. What is our extension rather than the bible's is the claim that the ladder's figure for a gate is the thing her condition defeats. That figure is authored and rises at every gate on the Body ladder, and the liver's entry says the rung-eight vessel has to be rebuilt rather than opened, so the arithmetic follows from the records rather than from an invented rule. Nothing here adds a mechanical consequence the records do not state.

art.palette_notes: Ash-grey and iron-blue lattice under an ember wash. The mineral reads matte and cold at the shoulders and forearms, the fire circulation reads as a slow orange bloom in the chest and throat. No polished highlights: nothing about her reflects light back, it absorbs it. Under-colour a dull oxide red where the two halves meet.

appearance.presentation: A dense, slow frame assembled for load-bearing work. Broad, low, and heavier at the trunk than at the extremities, as though the design's centre of gravity were placed rather than inherited.
appearance.age: Early in the long middle of a stoneborn's span. He reads as older than he is and younger than a soft body would at the same mark.
appearance.build: Broad and low with a heavy trunk and a deep ribcage: the most endurance available anywhere and the shortest reach.
appearance.complexion: Granite grey, faintly warm low in the trunk where the density sits, cool and matte everywhere else.
appearance.hair: Thin, dark and pressed flat, which on a frame this dense has nowhere to stand up.
appearance.eyes: Small, deep-set and patient, and set at an angle that reads the floor rather than the faces.
appearance.palette: Granite grey, ochre, iron, and a low ember bloom at the base of the throat.
appearance.attire: High-collared work coat of thick grey cloth, sleeves down and fastened at the wrist, iron collar worn under the coat against the skin.
appearance.marks: A wide shallow callus across both palms, and blue ore dust worked so far into the creases of the right hand that it has stopped being dirt.
appearance.bearing: Settled, unhurried, and slightly ahead of himself: the weight goes forward before he moves, and nothing about him is ever in a hurry to be anywhere.

canon.role_in_story: The Body ladder states its own premise twice and both statements are about becoming something other than what you were. Foundation is priced as the moment the frame stops being the body it was born in. Core Formation, the gate above it, is described as the first place a body can be built around something other than habit. Corst Belm is the one body in the setting that arrived at the ladder having already made that change. He is a dense, slow frame assembled for load-bearing work, and the assembly is the reason for the density: he was built to be loaded from outside, which is the most reliable account of why a stoneborn is stone rather than merely slow. Everything the ladder sells is available to him and nothing the ladder sells can be taught, because a curriculum is made of changes and he is living proof that the change is optional. He is unaffiliated, and the reason is not a wall. It is that every rung on the ladder is something his body already did, and there is no office in this setting for a man who has finished the argument before he starts.
canon.first_appearance: He appears in nobody's tally. A Foundation trial is held on flat ground on the plains, chosen for flatness rather than for ore, because the frame is set first, and Corst Belm is standing at the edge of that ring as the frame is set, having been asked to hold one end of a settling strap for four hours and having held it for four hours and then some, in the specific way that a stoneborn holds: without adjusting. The reader taking the standing weight at the ring looks at him, and cannot find a reading that matches anything she has weighed, because she is looking for a body to put in a column and he is looking at the strap. He is in the scene for eleven minutes and is described by two different observers as the most solid thing on the ground, which is praise on the plains and an injury almost everywhere else.
canon.lore:
A stoneborn is a dense, slow body assembled for load-bearing work. It carries more physique and stamina than anything else in this setting. It stops at the Immortal tier, because the density that makes it durable is the same density that will not let a dantian form. That is the whole species in two clauses, and it is why the record has almost nothing else to say about it: the density is simultaneously the reason the body is worth having and the reason it cannot do the one thing the body's own gates are built around.

Now read the ladder against that. The Body path is the one path that spends no charge at all; its entry gate costs nothing in qi and opens four vessels, and what it buys is not strength but structure. Its description says the change at the entry is the grain of the composition: the frame stops being the body it was born in. Two gates up, the Core Formation entry says a dense core forms where the ribs meet the spine, and calls it the first place the body can be built around something other than habit. That is the ladder's whole theory of development in one phrase: the seat of the self is where you stop being the shape you arrived in and start being a structure.

Corst Belm has been a structure since he was born, and he was not built by himself. He is broad and low and slow, and the density in him is load-bearing density, which is a different thing from the density the ladder produces, because the ladder's density grows from the inside outward around a spine and his grew from the outside inward around a load. He has never needed to be anything other than what he is. He has held a strap for four hours without adjusting. He has walked out of ground that took softer bodies, because a body built to bear is a body that does not go over.

And that is the whole problem. A curriculum is a sequence of changes, and a discipline is a set of states to be reached. He is in a body that reached the state the ladder is selling, at a rate the ladder never asked for and by a route the ladder did not author. There is no rung he can be shown as a step toward, and no teacher in this setting can demonstrate a transition to him, because the demonstration requires a person who has not made it yet. He is not excluded. He is simply already on the far side of the first sale, and nobody has built an institution for the person who arrives early.

What he has instead is the ceiling nobody has explained. The densest bodies stop at the seventeenth gate, one short of the end of their own tier, and the only account of why is a stonecutter's, held by a mortuary college that will not corroborate it because corroboration needs a second body. A stoneborn is what a dense body looks like when it is made deliberately rather than by selection, so the wall is written in his frame, and the record is careful to say that the composition reading and the practice reading make the same prediction from inside a complete composition, so nothing observed so far can separate them. He is the best evidence anyone has and he is not evidence, because nobody has taught him to make a claim he could be examined on.

The cost is the same fact and it is not a small one. He is the most enduring body available and the least trainable, because endurance is what the crossing gave him in place of the thing the ladder is made of. He has never been in a room where being slow was a cost rather than a fact. He will do anything asked of him, at the pace his frame sets, without complaint and without the option of a different pace, and there is no institution here that knows what to do with a body that cannot be improved and does not need to be.
history: He came out of a long line of stoneborn held deliberately for load work on ground chosen for flatness, the same reason a Foundation trial is held on flat ground, and the resemblance was never pointed out to him by anybody who noticed it.
From the first season he held the settling straps at a frame-setting, because a stoneborn is the body the frame is set against and the work finds him before he is asked for it.
He asked once, at a ring, to be shown what a practitioner does that he cannot, and the person demonstrating stopped halfway and started again, and he understood that the restart was the answer.

He was walked out of a cut face that took softer bodies, at his own pace, and came out of it carrying the strap he had been holding, which the record of the incident describes as an error by the rescuers.

He took work that asks a body to hold and stopped asking to be taught anything. The change was not announced and no form records it; he simply declined the last offer and has not been offered one since.

personality.summary: The most patient body on the plains and entirely unaware that patience reads as a virtue. He does not understand why anyone makes a fuss about the frame he has, because from inside it the frame is not an achievement, it is the shape he arrived in.
traits: Finishes what he has started, at a rate that has never once been a question.
Cannot be surprised by effort, and shows it by treating everyone else's effort as a matter of degree rather than of kind.
Answers questions about himself by describing the task, on the honest grounds that he does not have a second description.
Never asks for anything twice, having found once that nobody remembers an ask.
mannerisms: Settles his weight before he moves rather than during, which makes every motion of his look deliberate to a soft-bodied observer.
Reads a room by looking at the floor, which on a stoneborn means reading the load-bearing surface rather than the people's faces.
Does not interrupt, not out of courtesy but because interrupting requires a decision he can make instantly and he cannot.
Wears his iron collar inside his coat, against the skin, where it is functionally part of the frame.
motivations: To find the one thing his body can do that a body's own frame cannot, having looked for a long time.
To be measured by something rather than merely weighed, since being weighed is the only thing that has ever happened to him.
To be useful in a way that does not require him to be still, which is the one condition he cannot meet.
To see the seventeenth gate explained, being the frame that would be the evidence if anyone were permitted to examine him.
flaws: Cannot conceive of himself as a subject of instruction, so he cannot describe what he would need in order to learn.
Assumes every soft body is fragile, and has once handled a person with a care that was closer to a caution than a touch.
Cannot decline work by refusing it, only by waiting, which makes his no indistinguishable from a slow yes.
Has no vocabulary for his own condition, because nothing in his life has ever required him to have one.
personality.voice: Extremely slow, concrete, and almost entirely about materials. He says what a thing is made of before he says what it does. He has no abstract nouns in frequent use and the absence is not a affectation; there has never been a situation in which one would have been faster.
taboos: Being told he is exceptional. In his experience being exceptional and being handed more load are the same event.
Any teaching framed as a before and an after.
Iron used on the body for any purpose other than work.

relationships.note: It calls the dense core the first place a body can be built around something other than habit. He was built around a load. The sentence is the clearest account in the record of a thing he finished before he arrived.
The entry gate's stated content is that the frame stops being the body it was born in, and that is the only description in the record of what a stoneborn is.

It is not an organ and cannot be thickened like one, which the record says is exactly what a dense body needs and cannot get anywhere else. He carries more than anything here and has no pipe of his own to carry it in.

Exactly one account survives and it is held by a college that will not corroborate it, because corroboration needs a second body. He is the frame that would serve, and he cannot be examined because he cannot make a claim.
The network closed at Spirit Sovereign, so a frame this dense has no twenty-first conduit to open. He is the standing argument that the closure was not the cause, and he is not permitted to make it.

The trial ring is chosen for flatness rather than for ore because the frame is set first. He has held the strap that sets it, and the reading taken at that ring has never matched anything he has weighed.

reference_stats.summary: A frame that holds. Everything he does, he does past the point where it stops being interesting to watch, and nothing he does can be improved, because improvement is a change and there is no change in him available. He is the strongest body on the plains for the same reason he is the least teachable: he was built to take a weight from outside and never asked to carry anything himself.
strengths: The greatest endurance of any body here, which in practice means he finishes a thing no one else finishes rather than finishing one thing well.
A total absence of the frailty that makes soft bodies lose a contest, so he wins anything decided by who is still standing.
A frame that does not vary with load, which makes him the natural standard against which another body's capacity is measured.
A physical authority that settles disputes without speech, in a culture where the mark left standing is the only enforceable claim.
weaknesses: No rate of his own choosing. Everything he does is done at the pace his frame dictates and he has no mechanism for going faster.
Cannot be taught, which removes every advantage that instruction would give and leaves him with exactly what he arrived with.
No paired organ set, so the interior path is closed to him and the density that gives him everything also gives him one wall.
Cannot fight well and has never needed to, which makes the one moment his body is genuinely tested the one moment he has no instinct for.
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not read him as a wall and do not read him as a fighter. He is a duration. Put weight on him and he will still be there when the weight gives up, which means the encounter is decided entirely by what the opponent can do before it tires, and the whole of his danger is that he never participates in that decision. An opponent who tries to move him has chosen a contest about the floor. An opponent who simply waits has chosen one about the sun.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is one record sentence and nothing has been added: the density that makes a stoneborn durable is the same density that will not let a dantian form, so the endurance and the wall are the same fact. Our extension, and it should be read as ours, is the claim that a frame built around an external load has already made the change the Body ladder is priced on. The two descriptions the ladder offers are authored and quoted, and the reading of them here is ours. No mechanical rule has been invented: nothing in this record adds a consequence the race and cultivation records do not state.

appearance.presentation: A body built to breathe rock. A chambered nasal sieve behind a thickened face, a crop for grinding, a dermis like cured hide, and grey pitted enamel that no diet explains.
appearance.age: Some way into the long span of a belt body, and carrying a liver that is further along than the rest of her.
appearance.build: Low and broad through the chest with the heavy shoulders of a body that grinds rather than lifts; genuinely dense under load and better for a hard season.
appearance.complexion: Ash-brown with a dark mineral cast at the wrists and throat, and a permanent warm dust tone in every shadow on her.
appearance.hair: Coarse, dark and permanently half-full of grit, cropped because a body that overheats loses the only advantage it has.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and dark, lids thickened and lashes short to keep dust out; she reads air the way a sight-based body reads a room.
appearance.palette: Volcanic grey-brown, pitted grey enamel, iron black, warm ochre dust.
appearance.attire: High-collared coat of layered ash-grey canvas over long sleeves, a wrapped cloth at the throat, and a front pocket for samples worn through at the seam.
appearance.marks: A pale seam across the lower throat where the resting strain sits, and the grey furring of the tongue that the belt treats as an ordinary finding.
appearance.bearing: Nudged constantly into the wind, standing at the front of things, chin lifted and the whole body turned into the air rather than away from it.

canon.role_in_story: The Body ladder's own record of the rung-eight gate is two sentences and the second is the one that matters: the liver is the last ordinary vessel to open, it is the one that has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened, and a body whose vessel is damaged can still cultivate and simply stops being able to. The ashwalker ceiling is that gate, and the mechanism is arithmetic rather than mysterious: the mineral load in their blood settles on the liver first, and the liver is the first organ to fail under it, so they stop one step short of the reservoirs because they cannot hold the last ordinary meridian. Ostre Kesh's species therefore has a practice and a ceiling that are the same organ. Every step up would cost the thing that would have permitted the next one. She has taken none, and the reason she can say so precisely is the reason nobody else on the belt can: she can tell, to the year, what the organ looks like now. She is unaffiliated because there is no third description available for her: not a closed path, not a refusal, and not a rarity, but a body whose currency is the organ its own progress would destroy.
canon.first_appearance: She appears in a queue, at the front, and the scene is built around what she can do with her face in open air. The belt grades a household's contribution by running the grader's sieve against what the household brings, and the queue is the only place on the ash belt where two grades are compared in the same breath and permitted to disagree. Ostre Kesh is the body that compares them. She is first in the line because the register requires her to be, and the register has never made her a member of anything, and when the clerk reaches for a second signature she supplies the reading instead, aloud, in a voice pitched for a face rather than for a room. She has done this for years. No document records her doing it. The only written trace is a column of figures, entered in the same hand as the figures, with no name against hers.
canon.lore:
An ashwalker breathes volcanic grit and keeps it. The chambered nasal sieve is lined with cilia that trap grit and pass it into a crop for grinding, the dermis is thickened, and the blood is dark with suspended mineral. Smell is effectively gone and replaced by the sieve's direct contact sense, which is why the belt treats her kind as an instrument rather than as a population: they can tell two ash grades apart by tongue where nothing else alive can, and they process stone into protein, which is the only reason the ash-fall belt has a food chain above the lichen at all. Enamel is grey and pitted from grit rather than from diet. Everything about the design is a solution to one problem and the problem has a price.

The price is written on the same record and it is not hidden behind anything. The mineral load settles on the liver first. The liver is the last ordinary vessel on the ladder and the one that has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened, which is the only reason the rung-eight gate costs twelve vessels and not thirteen. So the eighth gate and the species' ceiling are the same organ, and the ceiling's mechanism says in as many words that they stop one step short of the reservoirs because they cannot hold that last ordinary meridian. What the ladder's own entry adds is the sentence that turns a wall into a condition: damaged, a body can still cultivate and simply stops being able to.

This is the whole of why she is not on a path, and it is worth being exact about it, because it is not the usual kind of exclusion. Her qi constitution is complete and durable. Her frame is complete and genuinely dense under load. Neither is closed to her and neither is refused. What she has is a price that is denominated in the same currency as the ladder: every step forward would be paid out of the organ that would have authorised the step after it, so the practice would not fail, it would be spent, and it would be spent before there was anything to show. She has not paid it. The arithmetic is a curve in which each success would reduce what is left to attempt one, and the reduction would be silent, because the belt's arithmetic is written in weights and grades and not in anybody's remaining capacity. A body whose gates would cost more than hers has an ordinary curve. Hers is one she has decided not to enter, with the whole of her species' reasons and none of her own to hide behind.

The paired cost is the same organ seen from the other side, and it is worse. The sieve is the reason the belt eats at all, and it is also the reason the belt is short-lived: any airborne toxin the sieve does not recognise is a wound, and there is no second line. One advantage, one instrument, and a single point of failure in the same place. She reads the air better than anything alive and cannot survive a whiff of a soft poison, and she has known this her whole life without it ever once changing what she does with her face.

The rest of the condition is social and it is not a small part of the answer. Conception holds only for a pair who stay within sight of each other through the ember season, which sets their whole spacing, and the recovery rites are laborious because the soul sits low and heavy and is hard to lift clear. So there are no dense settlements, no teachers in the ordinary sense, and a population that is scattered across a belt by its own reproduction. The belt's one rite of entry is the conversion itself, and that is a fact about the belt rather than about the ladder.

What she does is the one thing that is unambiguously hers. She grades. She stands at the front of a line in open air with an instrument no substitute exists for, and the register's accuracy is her body's willingness to be at the front. The register has never put her on a roll, has never written a name against her figures, and has never once had to, because the column is accurate. She is not asked and she is not refused. She is simply the most necessary body at the front of a line and the only one in the setting whose advantage and her weakness are the same organ.
history: She was graded as a child, at the front of a household's line, because the sieve works before it is trained and the belt does not wait for a body to be ready.
She took her place at the register's front and stayed there, in open air, in the season when the air is worst, for as long as the register has kept a column she was permitted to fill.

She has never gone near the last ordinary vessel, which for her kind is the wall and for everyone else is a rung, and the organ it would have to rebuild is the same one her sieve has been loading since she was a child.

A household brought in a load with a soft airborne component she could not name, and the sieve did not recognise it, and the record of that day contains the only injury her kind is known to take on this belt.
She resumed the front of the line on the next working day, at the same hour, and has not since asked to be seated, listed, or paid under any heading at all.

personality.summary: Enormously good at one thing, entirely without leverage from it, and cheerfully incurious about the arrangement. She has the settled cheer of somebody who has been told what she is for and agrees with the instruction, and she finds the politics of the belt faintly puzzling because from the front of a line none of it is load-bearing.
traits: States a grade plainly and does not soften it, because a softened grade is a wrong grade and the register has to publish it.
Trusts her own palate absolutely and will not take a reading from anybody else, on the sound basis that nobody else has one.
Remembers every figure she has ever entered, which nobody has ever checked and which has never once been wrong.
Finds the idea of being owed something faintly embarrassing and declines offers of thanks before they finish being said.
mannerisms: Chews the outside of her cheek when concentrating on a sample, so the grade is worked and tasted in one motion.
Keeps still in a heat that makes softer bodies move, on the theory that movement stirs the air and stirring ruins a reading.
Turns her face into a wind rather than away from one, and can be found by standing where the wind is worst.
Answers questions about the belt by putting her tongue to something, which she does not notice doing.
motivations: To be accurate, which is the only motive she has ever had and the one thing about her that has never needed defending.
To have her name on the column she fills, purely so that a future correction would be traceable to a person.
To see whether the last ordinary vessel can be held, knowing that the answer she is carrying is no.
To keep the belt fed, which is the one ambition available to her and which she has never described as ambition.
flaws: Cannot be given a qualification, because the belt's grade is the only competence it recognises and it grants none.
Will accept any exposure on the grounds that she has done harder work in worse air, and has no way of ranking her own risk.
Cannot refuse a reading on political grounds, and does not understand a question asked for reasons other than the grade.
Understates her reading's value in every transaction, because a reading that is obviously valuable is a reading somebody will try to own.
personality.voice: Rapid, concrete, and organised around samples. She describes the world in terms of what it would grade as, and her comparisons are all to other things on the belt rather than to anything in a metaphor. She is funny without knowing it and does not notice that the belt finds her funny.
taboos: Being seated behind the line. She will take the front or nothing.
Anyone handing her a figure to enter that she has not graded herself.
Soft ground. She has no second line and she has no reason to think she needs one.

relationships.note: It is the last ordinary vessel, the one rebuilt rather than opened, and a damaged vessel leaves a body that can still cultivate and simply stops being able to. Her species' entire ceiling and its entire cost are this one entry.

On the qi path it is where refined charge is kept between gates, and loss there is survivable and irreversible. She keeps everything her sieve takes and there is no organ in her line for returning any of it.

Its only window is a qi tide lifting the floor value, and her qi arrives through the same filter as the air she breathes, so the floor she stands on is loaded by the belt rather than by anything she did.

A strained law spends everything pushed into it and returns the floor reading. Every gate on the ladder is a round trip, and hers is the one body on the belt that has no route by which anything gets back out.

The entry gate's stated content is that the frame stops being the body it was born in. Hers never had soft tissue to stop being, which is why the advance costs her the organ that would have authorised the next one.

A scavenger reads a qi gradient through ash at a distance no sight-based predator can match, and she is the one body that can say what that gradient contains. Neither of them can do the other's work and both are built out of the same belt.

reference_stats.summary: An instrument with a body attached. What she does is read the air, and she does it better than anything alive on the belt, and every part of her advantage is made of the same material as the thing that will eventually take her. She is not slow and she is not weak. She is priced in an organ, and the ladder is priced in organs, and that is the entire collision.
strengths: The finest available discrimination on the belt: she separates two falls the eye has already agreed are the same, and no instrument can do it for her.

A qi constitution that is complete and durable and processes through the same filter as her air, so a practitioner with something worth spending has no better ground on that belt than she is standing on.
A genuinely dense frame that is better under load after a hard season, so the belt's worst days are her good ones.
Absolute accuracy, and a memory for figures no one has ever audited, which makes her column the one part of the register that has never needed correcting.
weaknesses: A hard wall at a low gate, and the wall is the organ that the gate itself has to rebuild, so the ceiling and the cost are the same tissue.
No second line against anything airborne that the sieve does not recognise, which is the majority of what a belt produces when something goes wrong.
Immobility and dependence on a mineral source: a quiet decade on the arc is a slow decline, and she cannot relocate to a cleaner belt without losing the only expertise she has.
Social spacing fixed by her own reproduction, so she has no household, no teacher, and no line of practice behind her of any kind.
reference_stats.combat_read: Read her as the most dangerous person at the front of a line and almost nobody at the centre of one. She has the density to hold and the durability to outlast, and she has no instinct at all for the middle of a fight, because the register has never asked her to be there. If the encounter begins in air she will read it before it decides anything. If it begins at contact range, the sieve's single point of failure is the only fact that matters.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is entirely authored and nothing has been added to it: the mineral load settles on the liver first and the liver is the first organ to fail under it, so the same load that lets her species process stone into protein is the load that costs them their ceiling; and the same sieve that is the belt's only food chain is the belt's only unrecognised-threat surface. Our extension is the reading that the ladder's rung-eight figure, which is authored, and the liver's rebuild clause, which is authored, together describe her condition as a price denominated in the ladder's own currency. That is an interpretation of two records, not a new rule, and no consequence has been added that those records do not carry.

Ash sits in the palette permanently: a warm, low-contrast dust tone in every shadow, because there is no shadow on the belt that does not contain it.

appearance.presentation: Long-legged, low-headed, plated and matte: a heat-dissipating skull, a second stomach for fermentation, a tail-counterbalance rather than a manipulator, and forelimbs that carry all of the mass.
appearance.age: In the early prime of a scavenger's span, which is never long and is never measured by anybody who was not counting.
appearance.build: Deep-chested and long, the spine running level from the plated skull to the root of the tail, with no hindquarter girth to speak of, which the record names as the wall his kind meets.
appearance.complexion: Ash-dusted charcoal over grey-brown, the muzzle and forelimbs carrying the only warmth, as though the parts that touch the aftermath are the warm parts.
appearance.hair: Coarse bristle along the spine and tail, flat and grey with the same dust that covers everything on this belt.
appearance.eyes: Dark, wide-set and unblinking, set on a skull that reads pressure rather than light.
appearance.palette: Charcoal, ash grey, spent-ground brown, a dull warm ochre at the muzzle and forepaws.
appearance.attire: No clothing: a scavenger is not dressed and never has been. A collar has been on him twice and off him both times inside a day.
appearance.marks: A worn patch at the muzzle where the plate has rubbed the dust through, and a healed tear at one ear from something he has declined to describe.
appearance.bearing: Perpetually forward-leaning even standing still, head down and tail working, the whole line of the body already pointing at the ground.

canon.role_in_story: Everything about the order of the ladder reduces to one vessel. The kidney is described as the reason the ladder has an order at all, because nothing else in the body holds a resource across a gate; the bladder's whole work is bookkeeping, holding what the body has decided not to spend; the gallbladder stores rather than moves. Sabek Rundle's qi network is a fast single loop with no storage at all. He takes in residual qi out of ash and carcass at a rate nothing else in the setting matches, and there is nowhere in him for any of it to be kept, so no gate has ever been paid from him: a gate is settled out of something held across it, and he has never held anything across anything. His own species record prices the rest of it in six words, and those words are about his kind and not about him, because they describe what happens to one of them that does break through: their breakthroughs are early and terminal. He is the setting's clearest case of a body whose whole advantage is the exact thing the ladder is denominated against. He is unaffiliated because no institution here can enrol a body that keeps nothing, and because the only thing ever offered in exchange for that speed is a road whose first step is also its last.
canon.first_appearance: He arrives in a scene already working and is described by the instrument he replaces rather than by anything he does. A survey of a spent face needs to know when a working is old, and the spoil is the only thing left to read, and a gradient read through ash at a distance no sight-based instrument matches is the only method that survives the depth. Sabek Rundle is put down the slope at first light with no collar, no marker and no paper, because the register that would hold those has never once listed him, and he comes back up before the light has properly established with a figure that three separate surveys disagree with more sharply every time they are repeated. The observer's written remark is not about him. It is that disagreement is what makes a certification necessary, which means his first reading on that face created a demand for somebody qualified to settle it, and there is nobody to name.
canon.lore:
The ladder has an order for one reason and the record gives it plainly. The kidney is the vessel every tradition treats as the one that stores what refinement is for later, and its entry says the thing in one line: it is the reason the ladder has an order at all, because nothing else in the body holds a resource across a gate. Everything above that is bookkeeping. The bladder's work is holding what the body has decided not to spend. The gallbladder stores rather than moves. Capacity is the unit and holding is the mechanism, and a gate is a step because a step is something you arrive at with more than you left with.

An ashjackal's network is a fast single loop with no storage at all, and the record says what that produces without softening it: their breakthroughs are early and terminal. There is no reservoir, no organ standing between the intake and the output, and no place in the body where a charge can be kept past the moment it arrives. He takes in more than anything alive on that belt can take in, at a rate nothing matches, and it goes straight through.

Which means the gate is not a step for him and has never been one. A step is settled out of a reserve, and he has no reserve at any moment of his life, so there is nothing for a gate to be paid out of. He has cleared no vessel and opened no node, and the phrase the setting uses for his kind's rare successes describes what would happen to a body that found one: early, and terminal.

The wall would have been a shape in any case, and the ceiling's mechanism is worth reading twice for that reason, because it is not about capacity at all: a four-legged frame has no hindquarter girth with which to close the girdling vessel. So even the ground his kind reaches on a good day is a matter of its skeleton rather than of anything it failed to build, which is the second reason a practice of that shape has no institution that knows what to call it.

Everything else about the design is a solution to being fast, and the fastness is total. Olfaction is a map; he reads a qi gradient through ash at a distance no sight-based predator can match, and the pack relay carries a reading to the others within seconds. He follows carrion populations and does not precede them. He eats the aftermath and cannot take a healthy adult of anything, and he is removed from a live fight in under a minute. The other two paths are shut by the same two facts that make the qi path work: the brainplate dissipates heat and leaves no cortical folding for introspection, and a frame built to shed heat cannot be built to store it. The advantage and the wall are one organ.

The economics of that are what make him useful and unemployable at the same time. A gradient read at distance is the only method that works at depth, on a spent face, without going down, because going down is how most of the belt's readers come back broken. He is therefore the answer to a question nobody wants answered honestly: how old is this working. He answers it. And his answer creates a second requirement, because three surveys that disagree more sharply the longer they are repeated are exactly the condition under which a certification becomes necessary. His accuracy is what manufactures the demand for a qualification, and he holds no qualification, because there is nowhere in this setting to put one.

There is also the matter nobody at the field will raise. A breakthrough that is terminal means the moment of success and the end of the road are the same event. Everything an institution in this setting provides is a step: a teacher, a cohort, a seat, a curriculum, a successor. Offered to him, each of those is a promise of somewhere further to go. He would be enrolled into a road that he has already arrived at the end of, and he has never asked for any of it, and the field has never offered, and both halves of that arrangement are stable.
history: He came up on a leeward gradient as a young animal following the aftermath of something a great deal larger had finished, which is the only way his kind arrives anywhere.
He learned to read a face by standing in spoil, first because it was where the food was and afterwards because it was where the reading was, and the two turned out to be the same errand.
He took a face three times and produced three figures that disagreed, and the disagreement was noticed, and the noticing created a certification nobody could fill.

A body of his kind somewhere cleared something, and the field wrote it down as early and terminal, and he read the entry and understood that he was being told where his own ceiling stood. He has not attempted a gate since, on the arithmetic that a reserve is required and he has none.
He went back down the slope. He has been down every face on that belt since and has not been named on a roll, a warrant or a rate card by any of them.

personality.summary: Fast, incurious about his own future, and entirely without complaint, because nothing in his history has ever taught him to expect a step. He is not serene. He is simply finished, and has no vocabulary for the difference between being finished and being ordinary.
traits: Reads a gradient before he reads a room and does not distinguish between the two.
Has no interest in the ceiling on his kind and would not understand the question if asked it.
Takes the reading back regardless of whether anybody wanted it, on the grounds that not taking it would waste the errand.
Refuses nothing that is work and notices nothing that is a favour.
mannerisms: Circles a spoil heap once, always once, before he will put a nose in it.
Head low and tail used as a counterweight when he is concentrating, which reads as aggression and is arithmetic.
Turns to face whatever has just changed in the air, mid-stride, without breaking pace.
Sleeps in the lee of a face rather than in shelter, and is the only body on the belt that would rather be near a worked ground than away from it.
motivations: To be read, which is the one form of attention he recognises and which nobody has extended to him.
To be paid in the belt's own medium for a reading he gave away, on the grounds that it was not free to produce.
To see whether the next face agrees with the last one.
To keep following the aftermath, which is the only project his species has ever had.
flaws: Cannot hold a resource for any length of time, which in a place that pays by weight means he cannot hold anything at all.
Cannot fight, and knows it, and will nonetheless enter an encounter that is already decided because leaving is a thing softer bodies do.
Cannot stay where he is put, because his kind follows carrion populations and does not precede them.
Has no way to know he is at the end of his road, because nothing in him has ever had a road to be at the end of.
personality.voice: Short, present-tense, and organised around smell and slope. He reports what is there and what is under it. He has no tense for anything that has not happened yet and no pronoun for a group he is not currently part of.
taboos: A collar. He has never worn one that he did not remove inside a day.
Being called a dog, and being called anything that implies he was invited.
Ground with nothing dead on it, which is a waste of a good nose.

relationships.note: Its entry says it is the reason the ladder has an order at all, because nothing else in the body holds a resource across a gate. His network holds nothing across anything, and the order he can reach is therefore an order with no steps in it.
It holds what the body has decided not to spend. That is the ladder's entire bookkeeping principle, and it is the one thing his kind has no organ to perform.
On the qi path it is where refined charge is kept between gates. His is a network that only moves, and the faster it moves the more completely the charge is gone by the time anything could count it.
The entry gate draws breath down and holds it in a reservoir that has never held anything. Holding is the gate's whole content and it is the one verb his frame has no grammar for.

The liver is the last ordinary vessel and the one rebuilt rather than opened. His species stops short of the same point for a different reason entirely, and the record is careful that the two are not the same fact.

It exists because a body whose technique merely weakens is indistinguishable from a weak practitioner. He is the extreme case: nothing he does is weakened, it is simply finished, and the lexicon has no word for it.

reference_stats.summary: A reader with no capacity to hold anything, including a qualification. What he does is arrive first, be right about what is under the ground, and leave. What he cannot do is keep any part of it, and in a setting where a body's stored progress is the only thing anybody trades on, that is not a limitation, it is an exclusion with no form attached.
strengths: The fastest absorption of residual qi anywhere on the belt, taken out of ash and carcass alike, which makes him the fastest reader of a worked face that exists.
An olfaction that operates as a map rather than as a sense, giving him a range on a gradient that no sight-based method matches.
A speed and an evasion that come from the same heat-shedding frame, so being difficult to catch is not a separate purchase.
A total indifference to being in a place where nothing died, which makes him willing to work ground every other reader refuses.
weaknesses: No storage whatsoever, which removes the ladder's unit of account from his body entirely and is the reason no gate has ever been paid from him rather than a passing disadvantage.
A breakthrough that is terminal rather than a step, so the whole of what an institution can offer arrives after the event it is for.
Cannot take a healthy adult of anything and is out of a live encounter in under a minute, which makes him useless as anything but a reader.
Follows the aftermath and cannot precede it, so he cannot be stationed, rostered, or relied on to be in one place twice.
reference_stats.combat_read: Read him as the fastest arrival and the shortest fight. There is no inside engagement for him at all: he cannot close on a healthy adult and he is removed from contact in under a minute. Everything he decides, he decides in the approach and from a distance, and the encounter that goes wrong for him is the one that begins at arm's length. Against a body that waits, he is a reader with no second act.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is authored and nothing has been added: the heat-shedding frame is what gives the fastest absorption and is also what prevents storage, and the species record states in one sentence that the breakthroughs are early and terminal. Our extension is the reading that the ladder's stated reason for having an order, which is one vessel holding a resource across a gate, describes his condition exactly and from the other side. That is an interpretation of an authored entry rather than a new rule, and this record adds no mechanical consequence that the race and cultivation records do not state.

art.palette_notes: Ash-dusted charcoal over the grey-brown of spent ground, with a heat-dissipating plated skull rendered as matte plate rather than as bone. appearance.presentation: A saltfolk body slightly more gracile than the line it came off, with a shallower brine sac reading as a pale translucency across the ribs and a palate that any softer body would call ruined.
appearance.age: Born into the last viable generation, which makes her young for a species with no future and old for one with no second chance.
appearance.build: Slight and narrow, the frame almost under-built, the shins and wrists thin enough to read as a person's rather than a saltfolk's.
appearance.complexion: Bleached salt-white and pale brine-grey, mineral rather than sickly, with the shallow sac showing as a soft light under the ribs.
appearance.hair: Cropped close at the nape and temples, because a saltwrack overheats and the sac is the only advantage she has.
appearance.eyes: Pale, still and unhurried, set wide on a slight face with the patience of a body that measures concentration rather than weather.
appearance.palette: Salt white, brine grey, wet blue at the standing line, faint ochre in the shade.
appearance.attire: High-collared coat of pale canvas over long sleeves, hemmed short at the knee so nothing holds at the waterline, and soft shoes worn through at the sole.
appearance.marks: The pale rim of the sac across the lower ribs, and a line of dried salt at the wrist she has never scrubbed off because it is accurate.
appearance.bearing: Still to the point of stillness, weight settled, standing at the exact edge of a boundary and making the boundary legible by nothing but being on it.

canon.role_in_story: There are three complete descriptions of how a saltwrack cultivates and not one account of a saltwrack who has. Every path in their record is written the same way: complete, and never exercised at any scale. That is not a closed path. It is the opposite of one. Her kind is the only body in the setting whose three ladders are fully specified by other people's hands and entirely unattempted, and the mechanism is not mysterious at all. They never reached the wall, because they never got past a run of declining generations, and competence takes longer to earn than a famine takes to run, so there were never two of them competent at the same time. A discipline needs at least one person who has finished it. Ilva Serrat is unaffiliated because she would be the first. She is not outside the ladder. She is its first subject, and there is nothing above the entry rung to be taught.
canon.first_appearance: She is standing where a line is, which is her office and the whole of her office, and the scene is built out of the fact that nobody else can stand there. The dominion's territory is exactly its waterline, and the stranded body's whole habitat is the same boundary, and the line cannot be split because moving it up the shore is the only way to give them ground and is also the only way to remove every subject who can drink there. So the standing line is the prize, and it is disputed, and the body that stands on it is a party to the dispute by the sole fact of being able to drink above it. Ilva Serrat is on the line when she is first described, and the description given is not of a person but of a position: a small figure at the water's edge, very still, in the exact spot where a treaty says two things at once.
canon.lore:
The extinction here is of a kind the record does not enjoy repeating, because it has no hunting in it. The basin's brine was replaced rather than lost. Everything the clade was built to drink became poison to it and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty, and the replacement water was perfectly potable and fatal, and the replacement crust was food and was nothing. One element moved. A species that had no alternative to that one element had nothing left, and there was never any process for noticing, because their taste could read the new brine perfectly well and that is the detail nobody involved found useful at the time.

It failed on a schedule rather than all at once, in a run of declining generations, with the last of them viable only while the old brine held in one sealed sump. The wall was never what mattered. The wall is ordinal eleven, the same wall every saltfolk meets, where the brine sac splits the penetrating vessel, and their own record says plainly that they are recorded here because the wall was never the thing that killed them. They never arrived at it. They never got past the famine.

That is the whole of her, and it is the reason she is not on a path. Their qi is complete and was never exercised at any scale. Their body is complete and was never exercised at any scale. Their mind is open and was never exercised at any scale. Three specifications, written by people looking at a body, and no practitioner anywhere in the history of the clade to say whether the specifications are true. She is the answer to a question the record has been asking for three generations without knowing it was asking: whether a saltwrack can do any of it.

And the answer cannot come from teaching, because there is nothing to be taught from. Transmission requires a competent person and a receptive one at the same time, in the same place, while the first is still alive. Competence is measured in a lifetime. A famine runs in generations. Those two facts do not have to meet for the failure to occur; they only have to fail to meet once, and a run of three declining generations is more than enough chances. So the practice did not decay, and it was not suppressed, and it was never illegal, and there was never an institution to suppress it. There was only ever a gap between how long it takes to become good at a thing and how long good at that thing was allowed to be carried, and the gap closed by itself.

The paired cost is the same fact read from the other side, and it is the reason nobody thought to close it. Their single dependency was also their single competence. A saltwrack could do exactly one thing that nothing else on that basin could do, and could do it without effort, indefinitely, in any weather, and so was never under any pressure whatsoever to acquire a second. The famine that removed them was not a shock to a population with reserves; it was the withdrawal of the only input a body that needs exactly one input ever had. Being the best at one thing is not a defence of it. It is the reason there was nothing else to fall back on.

What she has instead is a boundary. The dominion's territory is its waterline, and her kind stops above the brine line, so the ground that would save them is the ground that would end them being the people the dominion governs. The line is the prize and it cannot be split, and the reason it cannot be split is her own body: she can drink on one side of it and not the other. She is standing where a treaty says two things at once, and she is unaffiliated because no arrangement on either side of that line can put her inside it. The flank vessels, the deepest ordinary pair, need two warm gradients held at once, and the brine sac is the second gradient, and it is the thing the substitution took.

Her advantage is real and it is the reason she is still standing: she can read a brine that no softer body can survive drinking, and a shallower sac than her parent line's, which means she tolerates a concentration that finished them. Her cost is the same fact: a body tuned to exactly one thing, in a place where that one thing was withdrawn without anybody deciding to withdraw it.
history: She was born into the last viable generation, on ground that was already chemically wrong and had been wrong for long enough that nobody was still arguing about it.
She outlived the sump, in the way her kind does, by tolerating a concentration her parent line could not, which is the only talent the substitution left her.
She stood on the line for the first time with an older relative and was told, once, what the salt could be read for, and was given no further teaching because there was no further teaching.

The dominion moved its waterline up the shore to admit other subjects, and the line she stood on stopped being a place she could live and stayed a place she could drink, which is the distinction that has governed her since.

She was offered standing on the line as a recognised post by both sides and refused both, on the stated ground that a post has an inside and she has not got one, and the refusal is the only thing either side has written down about her.

personality.summary: Extremely patient, physically fragile by the standards of her own kind, and privately certain that she is the first of something. She does not think she is important. She thinks she is early, and the difference is the whole of her.
traits: Reads water before she drinks it, every time, including water she has already read.
Holds a position without fidgeting, which on her kind is a physiological fact and which she has never thought to mention to anybody.
Asks what a thing is for before she asks how it works, which has left her better informed than most people who trained properly.
Turns down offers with a stated reason and no bitterness, and has never once given a softer answer than the one she means.
mannerisms: Stands with her toes at the waterline, which is not a habit but a requirement, and looks mildly surprised when told it is a habit.
Tastes a sample before she answers a question about it, so her replies come a beat late and she never notices.
Keeps her hair cropped close, because a saltwrack's sac is shallow and a body that overheats loses the one advantage it has.
Counts things aloud when she is working, in threes, and has no idea why and does not stop.
motivations: To find out whether the three descriptions of her kind are true, which is the only question she has ever wanted answered.
To stand where the ground is honest, which is why she will not take a post inside an arrangement she does not believe.
To be the person somebody learns the practice from, if it turns out there is a practice.
To keep a record, since there is no institution that would keep one for her and the alternative is that the famine becomes an accident rather than an arithmetic.
flaws: Cannot be corrected by anyone, because there is nobody who has done it, so every belief she holds is unchecked and she knows this and cannot act on it.
Physically slight and unable to endure what a heavier body would, which makes any plan that assumes a hard season optional.
Reads concentration rather than intent, and so takes literally things that are being said at somebody else.
Has no way to leave, and does not want to, and the two are so intertwined in her that she cannot tell whether she is staying or stuck.
personality.voice: Slow, careful, and full of precise distinctions that nobody around her has ever had use for. She says what a thing is not as often as what it is. She uses the word we almost never, and when she does it refers to a clade rather than to anybody standing nearby.
taboos: Rain. She is on the wrong side of it and has been since a childhood she will not describe.
Being asked what her people can do, in front of anybody whose opinion of her she would then have to live inside.
Any position with an inside. She has declined four and remembers all four.

relationships.note: It is her own body that makes the prize indivisible: the dominion's territory is its waterline, her habitat is the same boundary, and moving the line up the shore would give them ground and remove every subject who can drink there.

The record gives ordinal eleven as the wall every saltfolk meets, where the brine sac splits the penetrating vessel. Her clade is recorded as never having arrived at it, which is the sentence that makes her existence a question rather than a body.

The mortal tier's whole curriculum is a closed list of what a frame seats, and it exists because a three-slot frame cannot carry a fourth subject. Her clade's entire collapse was one dependency becoming unavailable, which is the same shape at a different scale.

It is worth nothing outside its own tier because a tide cannot be read on any frame below the peaks. Every ladder in this setting runs on something that had to arrive from somewhere, and her kind is the case where it did not.

It draws breath down into a reservoir that has never held anything, and its only window is a tide lifting the floor. She is the one body in the record for whom that description is the whole of the opportunity, because she has not entered the entry rung and there is nothing above it to be preparing for.
A saltfolk body, slightly more gracile, with a shallower sac. The shallowness is consistent across every specimen and is the only anatomical reason she is standing rather than lying in a sealed sump.

reference_stats.summary: A body that outlasted its own kind and has nothing to show for it. She is gracile, slight, and exceptionally well adapted to one substance, and she has no combat function of any kind because a body tuned to reading concentration has no use for being hit. What she brings to a scene is a fact nobody else alive can produce: the three descriptions of her species' cultivation are entirely untested.
strengths: Reads a brine that no softer body can drink, which makes her the only living instrument for the question everybody got wrong.
Tolerates a concentration that finished her parent line, so the shallower sac is a real survival and not a cosmetic difference.
Holds a fixed position indefinitely without fatigue or complaint, which on the waterline is the entire job.
Sustained attention that no trained body in the record matches, precisely because she has had nothing else to do with it.
weaknesses: Slight and gracile, with a lifespan and a hardiness well under what the neighbouring saltfolk carry, and no resilience whatever to a beating.
A deep ordinary pair that needs two gradients held at once, and the brine sac was the second gradient, so the flank is closed to her by the same chemistry that killed her clade.
Rain is functionally fatal rather than inconvenient, which makes any ordinary weather a scheduling problem.
No practice of any kind to fall back on, no teacher, no cohort and no institution, which leaves her entirely without a second line of every kind.
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not read her as weak; read her as irrelevant to force. She has no second line in a fight and no capacity for one, and the honest reading is that an encounter decided by contact is decided before it starts. What she does in a scene is refuse to be hurried and keep saying the specific thing nobody else has checked, which in a place where the published figures have been wrong for three generations is worth more than any posture.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is authored and nothing has been added to it: the single dependency is also the single competence, so the species was never under pressure to acquire anything else, and the famine was therefore the withdrawal of the only input a one-input body ever had. Our extension is the transmission argument, which is ours: competence taking a lifetime and a famine running in generations are both in the records as authored facts, and the claim that the practice therefore could not survive is a reading of those two facts rather than a new rule. No mechanical consequence appears here that the race, conflict and cultivation records do not carry.

art.palette_notes: Bleached salt-white and pale brine-grey, with the shallow sac reading as a translucency across the ribs. Gracile where other saltfolk are heavy: the silhouette should look almost under-built, and the pallor should read as mineral rather than as sick. Add a wet highlight at the standing line, because the whole of her situation happens at a boundary in water.
